title: The Promises of God
subtitle: What he promises, who to, on what condition, and when it is kept: already, in Christ, in us now, or still to come
summary: "For all the promises of God are 'Yes' in Christ" (2 Corinthians 1:20). This study gathers the promises by what they promise, from his presence to the resurrection, and puts the great covenants behind them: to Noah, to Abraham, to Israel at Sinai, to David, and the new covenant. Each promise is tagged with who it was made to, whether it comes with a condition, and when it is kept, so the Patterns chart can count how many are already fulfilled, how many are being kept in us now, and how many are still to come. Tags follow the words of the text; notes say where a promise made to Israel is taken up for the church.

categories.title: Fulfilled in Christ
categories.note: Where the New Testament says Jesus keeps the promise.

categories.title: Kept in the story
categories.note: Where Scripture records the promise coming true.

categories.title: Taken up for us
categories.note: Where the letters apply the promise to believers.

categories.title: Said again
categories.note: Where Scripture repeats or enlarges the promise.

facets.title: Who it was made to
facets.note: The people the promise is spoken to in its own setting.

values.title: One person
values.note: Abraham, Joshua, David and others, by name.

facets.title: When it is kept
facets.note: One promise can be kept in more than one way: begun in Christ, worked out in us now, finished when he comes.

values.title: Already, in the story
values.note: Kept within the Old Testament account itself.

facets.title: Is a condition attached?
facets.note: Whether the passage itself attaches an if: faith, obedience, asking, repentance, waiting.

views.note: Eight things God promises, from his presence to the life of the age to come.
